extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys and agents) before the USPTO; counsel involved in patent prosecution and related litigation
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Final Order describing practitioner obligations and the disciplinary rules that govern filing Information Disclosure Statements, handling documents subject to protective orders, required certifications to the Office, and the sanctions/processes for breaches. Useful for evaluating attorney conduct before the USPTO and understanding resulting sanctions and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing and filing IDS without review (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) & (b) via 10.23(c)(15))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner violated 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b), via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(15), by signing and filing Information Disclosure Statements in the Office without having reviewed any of the documents comprising the statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states that filing an IDS without inspecting the submitted documents constitutes a violation; such a filing can be considered a false certification to the Office. The Order specifically finds that Respondent filed six boxes of documents without ever having held, read, reviewed, or inspected them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of protective order / conduct prejudicial to administration of justice (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice by violating a protective order issued by a district court constitutes a breach of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explains that filing documents covered by a district court protective order (and failing to file them as confidential in the USPTO) led to public availability and contributed to a district court finding of contempt and an award of attorney fees and costs. The district court found that continued participation after access to confidential materials was a 'blatant violation' of the protective order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling a legal matter without adequate preparation (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not handle a legal matter without preparation adequate under the circumstances; failing to take reasonable steps to determine whether documents filed were subject to a protective order or to file such documents in accordance with customary practice violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites the practitioner's failure to take reasonable steps to determine confidentiality or to use available USPTO procedures (see MPEP § 724.02) as inadequate preparation under the circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification requirement when presenting papers to the Office (37 C.F.R. § 11.18(b)(2)(i), formerly § 10.18(b)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered practitioner who presents a paper to the Office certifies to the best of his or her knowledge, information, and belief formed after an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances that, inter alia, the paper is not being presented for any improper purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order emphasizes that a practitioner who submits an IDS without inspecting the submitted documents—i.e., merely acts as a conduit for another person—is considered to have made a false certification to the Office under this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file confidential documents properly (MPEP § 724.02 / USPTO confidentiality procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents that are covered by a protective order must be handled and, where appropriate, filed with the Office as confidential under USPTO rules; failing to do so makes the documents available for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order references MPEP § 724.02 as the customary and acceptable practice for filing confidential documents. It notes that the respondent did not file the documents as confidential, resulting in public availability and contributing to the protective-order violation determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on acting as a mere conduit for filings
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must not simply act as a conduit for another person's submission of papers to the Office without reasonable review; such conduct can amount to a false certification and violates the practitioner's obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order recounts the practitioner's statement that he was 'merely a conduit' and treats that posture as insufficient—filing on behalf of another without inspection is untenable under the certification requirement and professional obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and remedial procedures for disciplinary violations (public reprimand, probation, show-cause, suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary remedies may include public reprimand, a probationary period (here, 24 months), issuance of an Order to Show Cause if probation terms or disciplinary rules are violated, and possible suspension for up to 24 months following the show-cause process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order sets specific procedures: OED Director may issue an Order to Show Cause and grant 15 days to respond; after consideration, OED may forward materials to the USPTO Director to request immediate suspension up to 24 months. The Order also requires publication in the OED Reading Room and Official Gazette, notification to the client with affidavit of compliance, and dissolution/dissociation of USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates if suspended. The Office may consider this record in future disciplinary matters as an aggravating factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and reporting obligations following discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon issuance of a Final Order, the practitioner must provide copies to affected clients and supply the OED Director with affidavits and corroborating documents demonstrating compliance within specified timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, within 30 days the practitioner must provide a copy of the Final Order to the client (TCS) and within 45 days provide the OED Director with an affidavit and corroborating documents (e.g., a copy of the letter mailed to the client) demonstrating compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office's authority to publish and to use disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and in the Official Gazette; the Office may consider the record of this disciplinary proceeding in any future disciplinary proceedings or when addressing further complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order mandates publication and explains that the Office may use the record as an aggravating factor in determining discipline in subsequent matters or in future proceedings, and that disciplinary decisions are posted in the OED Reading Room (URL provided).
